StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: One of the minority of AfterSideTurnEnd overrides the sim puts in the RIGHT slot: AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267) at CombatManager.cs:1256 for the enemy side, and on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345) is the sim's side-scoped enemy slot, fired once after every enemy has moved -- the same shape audit/records/power/tainted.json records. Amount: Zapbot.cs:37 applies HighVoltage 2 and monsters/glory/fabricator.py:101-102 applies _HIGH_VOLTAGE; non-ascension values, checked. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: MISSING `applier=`. C# passes `base.Owner` as the applier (`PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(choiceContext, base.Owner, base.Amount, base.Owner, null)`); the sim calls `PowerCmd.apply(self.hooks, self.owner, StrengthPower, self.amount)` with no applier, so `applier` is None through hooks.modify_power_amount (cmds.py:297), hooks.on_power_applied (cmds.py:327) and hooks.on_power_amount_changed (cmds.py:312), and the granted StrengthPower's .applier is left None (powers.py:59). Recurring gap shape 5 from the power stream's continuation prompt. DORMANT, and executed rather than asserted: the sim's only applier readers are RitualPower.__init__ (powers.py:195, an applier-side test that fires only when Ritual itself is applied), PossessStrengthPower/PossessSpeedPower._track (powers.py:3092-3099, which requires `applier is self.owner` AND `target.side == "player"` AND `delta < 0` -- this application targets an enemy with a positive delta), UnsettlingLamp (relics/unsettling_lamp.py:47, which requires `applier is self.player`), and the `creature is self.applier` on_death tests of shrink/constrict/dampen/hex (powers.py:1398, 1450, 3177, 3230), none of which is StrengthPower. Reproduce with `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py applier-readers`. Trigger: any future on_power_applied / on_power_amount_changed listener that keys on the applier of an enemy self-buff -- or porting Malaise/Resonance, which is power_cmd G1/G2's named trigger too. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

The sim substitutes `if not self.owner.is_dead` (powers.py:3252) -- recurring gap shape 8, a guard the sim changes rather than drops. The two are not the same predicate: a corpse the combat RETAINED is still a side participant in C# (the "death does not mean removal" finding; combat.py:292 keeps a retained corpse taking turns), so C# would grant it Strength where the sim refuses. DORMANT: the only ported retain-after-death mechanism is ReattachPower on Decimillipede segments (monsters/hive/decimillipede.py), which never carry High Voltage, and a dead Zapbot/Fabricator is removed outright. Trigger: High Voltage on a creature that is retained after death -- i.e. on a Decimillipede segment or an Illusion/Reattach holder, all ported classes.
